source_refs.note: 3. Structural Formula: a main subheading of 19.5 Representing Organic Molecules, its own page (owner 2026-11-04); PDF 45-46.

blocks.text: The structural formula not only shows the number of each kind of atom in the molecule but also the sequence in which atoms are joined together.
There are different types of structural formulae.
This formula is more complete and self-explanatory form of the structural formula.
“The formula which shows all the bonds between different atoms including the type of bonds as well as positions of functional groups in a molecule is called the displayed formula.”
highlight: “The formula which shows all the bonds between different atoms including the type of bonds as well as positions of functional groups in a molecule is called the displayed formula.”

blocks.alt: Displayed formulae with every bond drawn: butane, four C in a row with three H on each end carbon and two H on each middle carbon; ethanol, H-C-C-OH with two H above and below each carbon; ethanoic acid, H3C drawn with three H, joined to a C that has a double bond to O and a single bond to O-H.
blocks.caption: Displayed formulae of butane, ethanol and ethanoic acid (original drawing after the textbook's unnumbered figure).

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: Printed labelling slip: the three kinds of structural formula are labelled '(a) Displayed', 'a) Condensed' and 'b) Skeletal'; they are (a), (b) and (c).

Displayed formula uses a lot of space, it is very often condensed in to a one – line structure called condensed or linear formula. In this kind of formula, single covalent bonds are omitted, however, branches, functional groups, double or triple bonds and separating methylene groups in the middle of the molecule are shown in brackets e.g.
highlight: Displayed formula uses a lot of space, it is very often condensed in to a one – line structure called condensed or linear formula.

blocks.text: Skeletal formula is the simplified version of displayed formula which can be used to represent more complex organic molecules.

In skeletal formula, all the symbols of carbon and hydrogen atoms as well as the carbon to hydrogen bonds are removed. Bonds between carbon atoms are shown by single lines which meet at an angle. Each carbon is assumed to form enough C – H bonds to make a total of four bonds. Double and triple bonds as well as functional groups are shown in the skeletal formula. For example:

blocks.alt: Four rows, each with a name, a condensed formula and a skeletal formula: (i) butane, CH3-CH2-CH2-CH3, a zigzag of three lines; (ii) ethanol, CH3-CH2-OH, two lines ending in OH; (iii) methoxymethane, CH3-O-CH3, two lines meeting at an O; (iv) ethanoic acid, CH3-C(=O)-OH, a line to a corner with a double line up to O and a line down to OH.
blocks.caption: Condensed and skeletal formulae of butane, ethanol, methoxymethane and ethanoic acid (original drawing after the textbook's unnumbered figure).

blocks.prompt:
a) Draw the displayed and skeletal formulae of the following
i. 3,5- diethylheptane
ii. 2-bromo-3,3-dichlorohexane
iii. 2 – methylbutanal
blocks.explanation:
i. A seven-carbon chain with ethyl groups on carbons 3 and 5: CH₃CH₂CH(C₂H₅)CH₂CH(C₂H₅)CH₂CH₃ (C₁₁H₂₄).
ii. A six-carbon chain with Br on carbon 2 and two Cl on carbon 3: CH₃CHBrCCl₂CH₂CH₂CH₃.
iii. A four-carbon chain with CHO as carbon 1 and CH₃ on carbon 2: CH₃CH₂CH(CH₃)CHO.
In skeletal form each is a zigzag carrying these groups.

blocks.prompt: b) Draw the displayed and condensed structures of ethanol and methoxy methane, and explain whether they are isomers of the same molecule or not.
blocks.explanation: Condensed: CH₃CH₂OH and CH₃OCH₃. Both have the molecular formula C₂H₆O, but their atoms are joined in a different sequence (one is an alcohol, the other an ether). So they are isomers of each other (functional group isomers).

blocks.prompt: c) Draw the skeletal formula of ethanoic acid (CH₃COOH).
blocks.explanation: A short line (the CH₃ end) leading to one carbon; from that carbon a double line goes to =O and a single line to OH.
